summary: Harunaga Isaacson is an Indologist, Buddhologist, and Tibetologist. He earned an MA at Groningen and a doctorate at Leiden under Tilmann Vetter, Albrecht Wezler, and Hans T. Bakker. He held posts at Oxford, Pennsylvania (2002–2006), and Hamburg (2000–2002, 2006).

Harushige Takatsu was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and attended Oxford and Balliol College. He held multiple academic posts at the University of Tokyo from 1938 and became a professor at Musashi University in 1968.

Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson, alongside several other teachers. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-directed the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism.

Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia was an Indian historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He studied at University College London from circa 1934 to 1936 and served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from circa 1939 to 1973.

Haya Akegarasu was a Japanese scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and Shimei Futabatei at Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He later served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji and Shinshu Otani-ha.

Hayao Kawai was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1948 to 1952. He held posts at Tenri University, served as professor at Kyoto University (~1972–1992), and was director general of the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1995–2001).

Heather Stoddard is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1967–1970) under D. C. Lau, as well as under Nicole Vandier-Nicolas and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

Heeraman Tiwari is an Indologist and philosopher educated at the universities of Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford, where he completed his D.Phil. under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He has held faculty posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Heidelberg University.
Hege Myrlund Larsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bergen (attested 2009) under the supervision of Bruce Kapferer.
Hegoda Khemananda is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and as Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya (both attested 1993).

Heidi Fjeld is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Oxford and earned her doctorate under Signe Howell at the University of Oslo (~2001–2006), where she later worked as a postdoctoral fellow from circa 2006 to 2010.

Heidi I. Koppl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Copenhagen supervised by Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under the traditional teacher Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi Rika Maria Pauwels is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied at KU Leuven, Vrindaban Research Institute, University of Cologne, and University of Washington under Alan Entwistle. She taught at SOAS (1994–1996) and became a professor at the University of Washington.

Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen, Kerala Kalamandalam, and the University of Würzburg. She held positions at Tübingen from 2005, serving as Associate Professor and Managing Director of Indology (~2013), and visited Sapienza and Kerala Kalamandalam.

Heiner Eichner was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1967 to 1974. He held an academic post at the University of Vienna from circa 1989 to 2010.

Heinrich August Jäschke was a Tibetologist and linguist. He served as co-director at the Lehrerseminar der Herrnhuter Brüdergemeine Niesky in 1847 and worked as a missionary for the Moravian Church from 1857 to 1868.

Heinrich Blochmann worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history. He studied at Leipzig, Paris, and Calcutta, and held posts at Doveton College, The Asiatic Society, and Aliah University, where he served as professor and principal.
Heinrich Brunn was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1839 to 1843. He later held a post at the University of Munich from circa 1865 to 1894.

Heinrich Ewald was an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar educated at Große Schule and the University of Göttingen. He held professorships at the University of Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867) and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).
Heinrich Gustav Hotho was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1820 to 1826 and subsequently held an academic post there from circa 1829 until 1873.
